subject: Post-call: Reserved GPU qualification + two-phase scaling plan
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@cedarhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Reserved GPU qualification + two-phase scaling plan

Evan / Amelia — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth after the discovery:  

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Current LLM proof-of-concept is hitting noisy latency spikes under realistic traffic (p95 ~ 800ms for 2–3k token requests).
- Regulatory concern: PHI-related inference requires tenancy isolation and customer-controlled key management.
- Cost predictability needed for budgeting — your finance team prefers committed monthly spend over variable cloud spend.

Goals you called out:
- Production inference for clinical summarization and triage with p95 target <= 350ms for 512-token median workloads.
- Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pool) with VPC peering and KMS integration.
- Ability to burst for scheduled nightly batch jobs without risking noisy neighbor impact.

Suggested two-phase approach (what we recommended on the call):
Phase A (30–60 day ramp):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent slots (dedicated, no multi-tenancy) to hit baseline throughput for synchronous calls.
- Autoscale buffer: +2 slots available for burst (warm standby with fast provisioning).
- Network & security: VPC peering + KMS integration for model keys, audit logging enabled.
- Expected SLOs: 99.9% uptime; p95 latency target <= 400ms for your canonical prompt set.

Phase B (3–6 month scale):
- Expand to 8+ reserved slots based on telemetry and 95th percentile utilization.
- Add dedicated prefix & KV caching for common prompts to reduce token costs.
- Quarterly review and optional move to committed annual contract with better unit pricing.

Operational notes and assumptions:
- We’ll onboard with our Private control plane (managed by Redwood) in VPC mode; on-prem option exists if you need air-gap later.
- SOC2 docs and architecture diagrams attached.
- Pricing estimates in the attached spreadsheet are ballpark (we’ll lock numbers once we confirm reservation term and exact instance family).

Next steps we proposed on the call (action owners):
1) Redwood -> Evan: Send a concise reserved capacity estimate + SLA appendix (attached).
2) Cedar Health -> Evan/Amelia: Confirm preferred reservation term (monthly vs 12-mo) and expected start date.
3) Redwood -> Marissa/Monica: Prepare procurement packet and initial SOW draft (including KMS integration checklist).
4) Schedule a follow-up: 45-minute technical alignment next week with your infra lead — please share availability.

Attachments included: redwood_reserved_capacity_summary.pdf, capacity_estimate_2phase.xlsx, SOC2-Redwood-Attestation.pdf

If any of this is off, flag it and I’ll correct. If it looks good, Evan — can you confirm term preference and a target start week?

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Evan Park <evan.park@cedarhealth.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Torres <amelia.t@cedarhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Reserved GPU qualification + two-phase scaling plan

Thanks, Sergio — this is helpful and matches our notes. Quick clarifications from our side:  

- The p95 latency target you listed (<= 400ms during Phase A) is acceptable as a short-term goal; finance will push to 350ms if we move to an annual commitment.
- For isolation: we need dedicated tenancy (no shared hosts) and we will require KMS with a customer-managed key. Can you confirm Redwood supports HSM-backed keys via our KMS provider?
- Burst: the +2 standby buffer is fine, but we’d like an SLA for warm-up time when going from cold to warm (i.e., < 90s to reach provisioned capacity for burst).

Procurement ask: please send a formal quote for a 3-month pilot (monthly reserved billing) and a separate line-item for the annual commitment pricing so we can compare. Also include a short SOW so our procurement group can start an internal review.

Appreciate the SOC2 attestation in the attachments — our security team will follow up with a short questionnaire next week.

Best,
Evan
Head of Engineering | Cedar Health AI
ev an.park@cedarhealth.ai | +1 (503) 555-0102

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@cedarhealth.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Reserved GPU qualification + two-phase scaling plan

Evan — looping in procurement & solutions ops steps. Hello Evan / Amelia,  

We’ll prepare two artifacts by EOD tomorrow:  
1) Formal quote: 3-month pilot (monthly billing) + optional annual pricing line with committed discount.
2) One-page SOW: scope, deliverables, expected onboarding timeline, KMS/HSM integration checklist.

On the KMS/HSM question: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS and can plug into most cloud KMS providers. For HSM-backed keys we support integrations where the customer’s KMS exposes HSM-backed keys (we’ll include the integration checklist in the SOW).

Warm-up SLA: we’ll include a warm-provisioning commitment in the pilot quote — target < 90s to provision the standby buffer, with monitoring hooks for your infra team.

Action items:
- Marissa: send quote + SOW (owner).
- Sergio: schedule technical alignment (target next Thu 10–11am PT; Evan, please confirm).
- Evan/Amelia: share the name/email for the procurement reviewer so we can route the DocuSign and procurement packet correctly.

Thanks — we’ll get this into your inbox tomorrow.

Marissa Cole
Senior AM, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (312) 555-0147

--
Attachment stubs:
- redwood_reserved_capacity_summary.pdf (summary & assumptions)
- capacity_estimate_2phase.xlsx (line-item estimate, pilot vs annual)
- SOC2-Redwood-Attestation.pdf (attestation summary)
